summary: Iteration 2 backend regression + new feature tests for Mindful Companion. Added 9 new pytest cases covering: chat session auto_title from first user message, PATCH /api/chat/sessions/{id} rename (success/empty/404/cross-user), GET /api/chat/sessions?q= search, GET /api/integrations/telegram (verified VentBuddyBot enabled & polling), AI humanized prompt tone (no robotic openers), MongoDB session 'channel'='web' field, and the corrected consecutive-day habit streak (fresh log_today=True now yields streak=1, two same-day logs still streak=1). Total: 59/59 tests pass (50 regression + 9 new). Telegram bot confirmed running in backend logs as @VentBuddyBot via long polling.

minor.issue: Returns 200 OK even when the session does not belong to the user (silent no-op via id+user_id filter). PATCH correctly returns 404 in this case; DELETE should be made consistent (return 404 when matched_count==0) for ownership clarity.
Public endpoint (no auth). Acceptable for a public bot link, but worth confirming this is intended (no auth required).

action_items: (Minor, optional) Make DELETE /api/chat/sessions/{id} return 404 when session not owned/found, mirroring PATCH behavior — currently returns 200 silently.
critical_code_review_comments: auto_title (ai_service.py:253) truncates with rsplit on space then appends ellipsis; works well, but if first_message has a single 50-char word with no spaces, rsplit returns the whole 48-char chunk + ellipsis (acceptable).
rename_session (server.py:372) trims and caps at 120 chars and properly enforces ownership via {id, user_id} filter — good.

list_sessions search uses raw user input directly in $regex (server.py:365). User-supplied 'q' is not escaped, so regex metacharacters (e.g., '*', '(') from the user could throw a regex parse error from MongoDB or DoS via catastrophic backtracking. Recommend re.escape(q) before injecting into $regex.
delete_session (server.py:394) does not enforce 404 on cross-user attempts (silent no-op). Inconsistent with PATCH behavior.

Telegram bot is launched from FastAPI startup hook (server.py:732) — single-process pattern. If backend ever scales to multiple workers/replicas, polling will be duplicated and Telegram will reject overlapping getUpdates. For uvicorn --workers > 1 use a sentinel/lock or move bot to its own service.
CORS still uses allow_origins from CORS_ORIGINS env defaulting to '*' WITH allow_credentials=True (server.py:704-710). Browsers reject this combination — set explicit FRONTEND_URL for production.

PROFESSIONAL_SYSTEM and GENZ_SYSTEM prompts (ai_service.py:50, 104) are large multi-line strings; rebuilt every chat call inside generate_chat_response. Consider caching the joined system message to avoid re-concat per request (micro-optimization).

Chat session 'channel' field is set to 'web' on every upsert via $set (server.py:259). For Telegram-created sessions this would overwrite channel='telegram' if a web message ever lands on that session_id. Currently telegram & web session_ids don't collide (different prefixes), so safe — but document this assumption.
test_credentials: admin@mindful.app / Admin@123 (verified). Tests auto-register fresh users with @example.com domain.
seed_data_creation: Admin auto-seeded by backend startup. Tests create per-class fresh users (test_<uuid>@example.com) plus TEST_ prefixed habits, journals, moods, checkins, and chat session titles.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Use /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py — 59 tests, 100% pass, ~60s runtime. New TestChatSessionsV2 / TestAITone / TestTelegramInfo classes cover iter 2 features. Habit streak tests now assert true consecutive-day streak (fresh single log => streak=1). VentBuddy Telegram bot running as @VentBuddyBot in long-polling mode (verify via backend logs `grep 'polling as @' /var/log/supervisor/backend.*.log` and GET /api/integrations/telegram). Telegram message delivery itself cannot be tested from container — only the public info endpoint is validated.
rca of the issue: No blocking issues. Optional consistency fix: delete_session should 404 when not found/not owned. Minor security: list_sessions $regex search does not re.escape user input (could throw or cause DoS on adversarial input).
